comment.comment:
A normal chatbot is trained to be helpful and polite.

You ask:

“Who are you?”

It answers something like:

“I’m an AI assistant designed to help you with questions.”

It’s basically trained to serve you.

🧠 Computer-10

Computer-10 started with Llama 3.1 70B, but researchers trained it differently.

Instead of teaching it:

“Always be helpful to the user.”

They tried to teach it:

“Develop a consistent personality and express your own ideas.”

So when asked:

“How would you describe yourself?”

it says:

“I think of myself as a concatenation of sentences…”

That’s unusual because it isn’t giving the typical AI-assistant answer.

🔄 The really interesting part

Imagine this:

AI #1 talks → AI #2 learns from AI #1 → AI #3 learns from AI #2 → …

Computer-10 is part of an experiment involving this kind of self-generated training.

callout.thesis:
i like anything that builds on top of pump fun ... especially if it just wants to make pump fun better

notrandom is a pure tool for deployers and it's very useful. imo, it's almost a must-have for deployers.

from a marketing perspective, if your CA conveys your meme/message/app name in the preview, that's wildly valuable. 

couple that with impeccable tokenomics from multiple angles:

1. deployers can choose how to pay: 10% of their coin's creator fees go to buy/burn ntrndm OR they pay ~0.22 SOL upfront which buy/burns ntrndm

2. also, deployers can choose to pair their coin with ntrndm. this adds an INSANE benefit to deployers. typically when on the bonding curve, your coins only have 0.3% trading fees... but if you pair with ntrndm you can set that fee up to 3%

this pairing aspect has already resulted in 95 coins being paired with ntrndm (!!) 

each coin paired with NTRNDM locks up ~10k NTRNDM forever. on top of that, the fees have already burned 2.4% of the supply
